audits.title: 239 An Audit on The Consenting Process For Orthopaedic Surgery During The COVID Pandemic
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons COVID-19 consent guidance: all patients informed of COVID-19 risk (in-hospital risk 0.45%)
audits.setting: Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Hospital, Oswestry (orthopaedic surgery)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 risk documented on 44% of consent forms (56% not documented). Of forms without it, 34% completed by consultants, 18% fellows, 48% registrars.

audits.other_findings: 6% of patients were suspected of COVID post-operatively and tested; 0% contracted COVID.
audits.citation: Manoharan G, Edakalathur J, Akhbari P, Potter R. 239 An Audit on The Consenting Process For Orthopaedic Surgery During The COVID Pandemic. Br J Surg. 2021;108(Suppl 6).

audits.title: 406 Audit of Current COVID-19 Consent Process
audits.standard: Best practice for informed consent: patients made aware of risk of contracting COVID-19
audits.setting: Single orthopaedic unit (University of Glasgow affiliation); emergency and elective consent forms

cycle1.result: COVID-19 included as a risk in 21/51 (41.2%); elective 10/24 (41.7%), emergency 11/27 (40.7%).

audits.intervention: Results circulated to all orthopaedic staff as a poster, with 2 weeks of educational awareness.
audits.other_findings: Elective practice remained poor. One patient tested positive pre-operatively and one post-operatively.
audits.citation: Goldmann N, Brown C. 406 Audit of Current COVID-19 Consent Process. Br J Surg. 2021;108(Suppl 6).

audits.title: 85 A Closed Loop Audit of Consent for Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery in the COVID-19 Pandemic
audits.standard: Departmental guidance to specify COVID-19 as a risk on trauma and orthopaedic consent forms
audits.setting: Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow, Major Trauma Centre

cycle1.result: 49% of consent forms specified COVID-19 as a risk.

audits.intervention: Data presented at departmental governance meeting and an infographic disseminated to all clinicians.
audits.other_findings: Indicative perioperative COVID-19 risk fell from 2.15% (2 positives) to less than 1% (no positives).
audits.citation: Goh J, Neary C, Razii N, Little K, Leach W. 85 A Closed Loop Audit of Consent for Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery in the COVID-19 Pandemic. Br J Surg. 2022;109(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Use of abbreviations in consent forms for orthopaedic patients: A quality improvement project
audits.standard: GMC, Royal College of Surgeons Glasgow and British Orthopaedic Association guidance on consent
audits.setting: Level one trauma centres, orthopaedic trauma procedures

cycle1.result: Abbreviations used in 54% of consent forms.

audits.intervention: Results presented at morbidity and mortality meeting, generic email to all staff to avoid abbreviations, and advertising use of full medical terms.

cycle2.result: Abbreviations used in 22% of consent forms.

audits.other_findings: DVT and PE were the most common abbreviations.
audits.citation: Khan MN, Anjum S, Shafique H. Use of abbreviations in consent forms for orthopaedic patients: A quality improvement project. . 2024. doi:10.22541/au.170665488.84870109/v1.

audits.title: Assessing the adequacy of procedure-specific consent forms in orthopaedic surgery against current methods of operative consent.
audits.standard: Information on BOA-endorsed Orthoconsent forms as the set standard for patient understanding at confirmation of consent
audits.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells

cycle1.result: Patients consented with standard yellow generic forms scored an average of 56.7% (knee arthroscopy) and 57.6% (total knee replacement) on questionnaires.

audits.intervention: Patients additionally given the procedure-specific Orthoconsent form to read at home and sign on the morning of surgery.

cycle2.result: Average scores rose to 80.5% (knee arthroscopy) and 81.6% (total knee replacement).

audits.other_findings: 100 knee arthroscopy and 60 total knee replacement patients took part in total; questionnaires had 26 (KA) or 35 (TKR) questions.
audits.citation: Barritt AW, Clark L, Teoh V, Cohen AM, Gibb PA. Assessing the adequacy of procedure-specific consent forms in orthopaedic surgery against current methods of operative consent. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2010;92(3):246-9; quiz 2p following 249. doi:10.1308/003588410x12628812458257. PMID: 20412675.

audits.title: An audit of consent for allograft use in elective orthopaedic surgery.
audits.standard: General Medical Council guidance on consent; documentation of consent for allograft use
audits.setting: Musgrave Park Hospital, large elective orthopaedic unit with onsite bone bank

cycle1.result: 17/45 cases (38%) had adequate preoperative documentation or an appropriately completed consent form for planned allograft use.

audits.other_findings: Revision hip arthroplasty was the main allograft user (48%); little correlation between surgeon allograft use frequency and consent adequacy (correlation coefficient -0.12).
audits.citation: Mullan CJ, Pagoti R, Davison H, McAlinden MG. An audit of consent for allograft use in elective orthopaedic surgery. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2016;98(4):254-257. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2016.0070. PMID: 26924483.

audits.title: Improving consent in patients undergoing surgery for fractured neck of femur.
audits.standard: British Orthopaedic Association-endorsed consent guidance (12 potential risks)
audits.setting: Single centre; Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 4/12 risks documented in <50% of intracapsular fractures (n=35) and 7/12 in <50% of extracapsular fractures (n=35)

audits.intervention: Raising awareness and attaching consent guidance; neck of femur fracture-specific consent form then implemented

cycle2.result: 100% documentation of potential risks in intracapsular and extracapsular fractures

audits.title: Informed consent for surgery on neck of femur fractures: A multi-loop clinical audit.
audits.standard: BOA-endorsed consent guidance (orthoconsent.com); departmental standard of 100% documentation of common, less common and rare risks on Consent Form 1 for NOF fracture surgery
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Kettering General Hospital

cycle1.result: 2015 cycle: infection 100%, bleeding 87%, clots 93%, anaesthetic risks 53%, neurovascular injury 93%, pain 73%, altered wound healing 60%, non/mal-union 33%, failure of surgery 87%, mortality 40%, prosthetic dislocation 0%, leg length discrepancy 0%.

audits.intervention: Verbal and written dissemination of results, printed risk list displayed in the orthopaedic doctors' office, and amendments to the junior doctor induction handbook.

cycle2.result: Of 100 NOF patients, 48 with capacity (AMT ≥8) audited: infection, bleeding, clots and anaesthetic risks 100%; neurovascular injury 98%; failure of surgery 83%; pain 75%; non/mal-union 71%; altered wound healing 69%; mortality 21%; prosthetic dislocation 14%; leg length discrepancy 6%.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles (2015, 2016, 2019); 2016 values included anaesthetic risks 76%, pain 42% and mortality 61%. The 100% target was still not met; after the latest cycle the trust approved two consent-specific stickers (arthroplasty/fixation) and inappropriate abbreviations were noted.
audits.citation: Shah R, Sambhwani S, Al-Shahwani A, Plakogiannis C. Informed consent for surgery on neck of femur fractures: A multi-loop clinical audit. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2020;54:26-31. doi:10.1016/j.amsu.2020.03.008. PMID: 32461800.

audits.title: Improving the surgical consenting process for patients with acute hip fractures: a pilot quality improvement project.
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons consent standards
audits.setting: Royal Gwent Hospital, Newport; 774-bed district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics

cycle1.result: Procedure details documented 93%; abbreviations used in 38%; procedure-specific risks documented 31%; copy offered to patient 12%.

audits.intervention: Cycle 1 (January 2018): induction and departmental teaching on consent plus senior review of consent forms on the morning ward round. Cycle 2 (August 2018): hip fracture proforma with pre-printed procedure-specific consent risk stickers and induction teaching on their use.

cycle2.result: Procedure details documented 100%; abbreviations 7%; procedure-specific risks documented 67%; copy offered to patient 8%.

audits.other_findings: After teaching alone (January 2018, n=26) abbreviations fell to 20%, procedure-specific risks rose to 72% and copies offered to 48%. Sticker supplies ran out and formal use fell below 75% of forms, and offering a copy fell once it was not prompted.
audits.citation: Singh K, Assaf A, Bayley M, Gillespie G. Improving the surgical consenting process for patients with acute hip fractures: a pilot quality improvement project. Patient Saf Surg. 2020;14:26. doi:10.1186/s13037-020-00252-8. PMID: 32547634.

audits.title: Do we achieve the Montgomery standard for consent in orthopaedic surgery?
audits.standard: Montgomery v Lanarkshire Health Board (2015) standard for informed consent
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, Wirral University Hospital Trust (elective patients)

cycle1.result: Specific patient risks documented 50%; procedure-specific risks 42%; alternative options 48%; written information 14%.

audits.intervention: Results presented to clinicians and a teaching session on expected consent standards.

cycle2.result: Specific patient risks 60%; procedure-specific risks 76%; alternative options 66%; written information 8%.

audits.other_findings: Copied letters to patients in only 12% across cycles; dedicated consenting clinics outperformed standard clinics.
audits.citation: Tonge XN, Crouch-Smith H, Bhalaik V, Harrison WD. Do we achieve the Montgomery standard for consent in orthopaedic surgery?. Br J Hosp Med (Lond). 2021;82(4):1-7. doi:10.12968/hmed.2020.0504. PMID: 33914632.

audits.title: Use of abbreviations in consent forms for orthopaedic surgery: A pilot study.
audits.standard: GMC, RCS Glasgow and BOA consent guidance; no abbreviations on consent forms
audits.setting: Level one trauma centre, trauma and orthopaedics department (Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast affiliation)

cycle1.result: Abbreviations in 189/350 (54%) forms; mostly by registrars (74%); DVT and PE commonest.

audits.intervention: Results presented at M&M meeting, email to all staff, reminder sticker attached to consent forms and poster in areas where consent is taken.
audits.other_findings: DVT and PE remained the commonest abbreviations; use of CRPS, PIP and EUA rose in proportion.
audits.citation: Khan MNH, Shafiq H, Ilyas MW, Jamshed MH, Qureshi AI, Khan BG, et al.. Use of abbreviations in consent forms for orthopaedic surgery: A pilot study. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2021;71:102949. doi:10.1016/j.amsu.2021.102949. PMID: 34712478.

audits.title: Informed Written Consent for Orthopaedic Trauma in the Emergency Setting at a Tertiary Referral Centre: A Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.standard: American Association of Orthopaedic Surgeons 'Orthopaedic Surgical Consent' standards (name, DOB, board number, procedure without abbreviation, side/site stated); no target stated
audits.setting: Galway University Hospitals, tertiary referral centre; consent forms for emergency orthopaedic trauma surgery

cycle1.result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 79 (74.5%). Side/site 81 (76.4%) (the abstract wording says 'without correctly stating' but the comparison treats this as compliance). Abbreviation and side/site both failing in 13 (12.3%).

audits.intervention: A single 90-minute virtual education session for all trauma and orthopaedic staff on consent standards, sharing cycle 1 results.

cycle2.result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 37 (92.5%, p=0.02). Side/site correctly stated 39 (97.5%, p=0.0015). No form had both failures (0% vs 12.3%, p=0.02).

audits.other_findings: Only 106 of 147 and 40 of 57 consent forms were available for review. The abstract gives the cycle 1 sample as 107.
audits.citation: Davey MS, Davey MG, Mohan K, O'Driscoll CS, Murphy CG. Informed Written Consent for Orthopaedic Trauma in the Emergency Setting at a Tertiary Referral Centre: A Closed-Loop Audit. Cureus. 2021;13(11):e19460. doi:10.7759/cureus.19460. PMID: 34926032.

audits.title: Patients Lacking the Capacity to Consent to Hip Fracture Surgery May Be Undergoing Major Operations Without Their Next of Kin Being Involved in Best-Interests Decisions: A Quality Improvement Report.
audits.standard: Mental Capacity Act 2005 best-interests process; documented attempt to contact next of kin before surgery and completion of NoK section of Consent Form Four
audits.setting: 520-bed district general hospital trauma unit (Royal Surrey County Hospital)

cycle1.result: Documented attempt to contact NoK 80% (24/30); NoK section of Consent Form Four completed 30% (10/30).

audits.intervention: Feedback presentation at trauma meeting and email to orthopaedic team.

cycle2.result: Documented attempt to contact NoK 100% (28/28), p<0.05; NoK section completed 64.3% (18/28), p<0.05.

audits.other_findings: Registrar survey suggested the Consent Form Four NoK section is easily missed; planned consent e-training and form redesign.
audits.citation: Zalmay P, Collis J, Wilson H. Patients Lacking the Capacity to Consent to Hip Fracture Surgery May Be Undergoing Major Operations Without Their Next of Kin Being Involved in Best-Interests Decisions: A Quality Improvement Report. Cureus. 2021;13(12):e20322. doi:10.7759/cureus.20322. PMID: 35028219.

audits.title: Audit on the Adequacy of Consenting Practices for Neck of Femur Fracture Surgeries.
audits.standard: GMC Decision Making and Consent (2020), RCS England Consent: Supported Decision-Making (2016) and the BOA-endorsed orthoconsent.com model hip fracture consent form
audits.setting: St Richard's Hospital, Chichester; district general hospital trauma and orthopaedic department

cycle1.result: Infection documented in 98.4%, blood clots 95.2%, bleeding 92.1%, neurovascular injury 79.4%, dislocation 77.8%, pain 74.6%, anaesthetic complications 73%, failure 68.3%, leg length discrepancy 60.3%, bone damage/fracture 50.8%, death 49.2%, wound complications 42.9%, hip stiffness 14.3%, catheterisation 0%. Diagnosis missing in 22.2% (n=14), benefits in 12.7% (n=8), responsible consultant in 28.6% (n=18), blood transfusion in 25.4% (n=16).

audits.other_findings: 52.4% of consents were taken by SHOs/core trainees without formal orthopaedic training; orthopaedic-specific risks were documented less often than generic risks (p<0.00001). Patient name and date were missing beside the signature in 57.1% (n=36); induction teaching, governance presentation and posting the model form were recommended with a planned re-audit.
audits.citation: Perera H, Wusu AM, Mohammad A, Qulaghassi MZ, Adekola A, Rao M. Audit on the Adequacy of Consenting Practices for Neck of Femur Fracture Surgeries. Cureus. 2023;15(11):e48565. doi:10.7759/cureus.48565. PMID: 38024031.

audits.title: Looped quality improvement project of consent forms in patients admitted with hip fracture.
audits.standard: BOA standardised list of risks for NOF fracture procedures
audits.setting: Royal Oldham Hospital, Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Average of only 56.6% of risks included on each consent form; significant risks such as mortality frequently missed.

audits.intervention: Stickers for consent forms and team education sessions.
audits.other_findings: Authors recommend a further cycle to check sustainability.
audits.citation: Bharadwaj A, Morter R, Bonshahi A. Looped quality improvement project of consent forms in patients admitted with hip fracture. J Clin Orthop Trauma. 2025;60:102867. doi:10.1016/j.jcot.2024.102867. PMID: 39759464.
